title: Electromagnetic Spectrum and Atomic Applications
purpose: Relate wavelength, frequency, energy, and spectrum applications.
safetyNotes: Use spectrum diagrams and safe public data only. No lasers, discharge tubes, or flame tests without assignment.
simulationReview: Direct simulation/resource link is provided in P01.html and in directSimulationUrl.
simulationVirtualLabReviewRequirement: Required for atomic models, periodic trends, energy levels, and spectra
directSimulationTitle: PhET Models of the Hydrogen Atom
directSimulationStudentTask: After the simulation opens, use the hydrogen atom model and turn on the light or spectrum display if it is available. Compare at least two model views or settings that show electron energy behavior. Observe the emitted or absorbed light pattern and connect each visible line or color to an energy change. Record the model used, the spectrum evidence observed, and one sentence connecting quantized energy levels to Electromagnetic Spectrum and Atomic Applications.
simulationReviewImplementation: Student-facing lesson includes one exact direct simulation/resource link plus adjacent step-by-step directions for what to open, click/use, observe, record, and connect to the lesson standard.
simulationSourceReference: NASA EM spectrum resources; PhET; OpenStax Chemistry 2e
